source_snapshot.title: A Hacker Found What His Samsung TV Was Tracking
source_snapshot.content: Cybersecurity bounty hunter says that Samsung TVs use AI to record audio and screenshots for ads. Um hacker says, "Finally found a company that truly listens to its customers." Uh he goes by log4j and noticed that his 2025 Samsung TV was serving him weirdly targeted ads. So, as any good hacker would, he hacked his own TV to find out why, which by the way is totally legal. What he found was an on-device AI model that logs which YouTube videos he watches, which ads he skips, and how far into each one he gets. The TV also takes ACR screenshots, so basically it takes screenshots of whatever's on screen and ties it all into an advertising ID that supposedly follows him across devices. His other big find was an always-on sound sensor that counts dogs barking and babies crying and sends those counts back to Samsung, which already sells that detection as a pet and baby care feature. He claims TVs without a mic can go looking for one on a connected soundbar or Bluetooth speaker, and Samsung's own developer docs show that its TV software can find and switch on connected mics, though that alone doesn't prove that they are doing it. Log4j was using Codex, OpenAI's coding agent, to dig through the firmware, and OpenAI banned his account for cyber abuse, which he says cost him about $500. He thinks the work tripped OpenAI's daybreak cybersecurity checks, but the ban email didn't mention the TV, and OpenAI hasn't said what got flagged. Samsung has not responded, and he has promised a full write-up in the near future. >> Nice. This has been a wild saga with TVs. >> Mhm. >> I guess the part that surprises me most is are we surprised by this? I I everyone knew that they were doing this. I I I >> I think it's like to the degree I think is the >> I just assume everything is watching and listening all the time. Like I don't even pick my nose if I'm not in my bathroom at this point. Like it's just it like it's just it's it's gotten it's gotten it's gotten to that point, man. Electrobot says we didn't know the extent and I'm like yeah I I yeah I guess. I just I don't know I've just gotten so many creepy targeted ads over the years that even though it's been it's been quote unquote proven that like your your phone doesn't just transcribe everything that you say and upload it somewhere or whatever. I just kind of >> suspicious of >> I assume that at some point it will and no one's going to notify me so I might as well act like it does. I >> It's cool though with the awareness there's a lot of stuff coming. Like uh we we talked last week about um Vibe coded TV operating system replacements. >> Yeah. >> I don't know how effective those necessarily are currently but there's some projects getting some attention. Uh people seem to be continuing to contribute towards them. Uh they seem roll backable at least the one that I know of uh if you have any problems with it so maybe it'll help you. Maybe it doesn't. I'm not sure. Look into yourself but yeah.
